paragraphs.source_en:
The Wild Swans at Coole: first published in 1917, the volume including the play
At the Hawk's Well. Contents and order here follow the 1919 edition, which
added seventeen poems.
 143: Coole Park was the estate of Lady Gregory in County Galway.
 144: Robert Gregory (1881-1918), Lady Gregory's only child. A pilot in the
Royal Flying Corps, he was killed in action in Italy on 23 January 1918.
 144.1: see Yeats's note on "The Tower," pp. 459-6o.
 144.17: Lionel Johnson (1867-1902), English scholar-poet and critic.
 144.25: John Millington Synge (1871-1909), Irish playwright and friend of
Yeats.
 144.33: George Pollexfen (1839-1910), a maternal uncle of Yeats.
 144.34: a county in Ireland.
 144.39: astrological terms for heavenly bodies that are separated by 180°, 90°,
and 120°, respectively. Pollexfen was a student of astrology.
 144.47: Sir Philip Sidney (1554-86), English writer, statesman, and soldier.
